title: NVIDIA Kumo Relational Outperforms Supervised Machine Learning on Relational Data, No Training Required
script:
NVIDIA just released Kumo Relational, a new foundation model for tabular data.
It predicts outcomes on relational databases without any task-specific fine-tuning.
Kumo uses graph neural networks to map complex relationships between table rows.
Researchers trained the model on massive synthetic data to learn general relational patterns.
This architecture eliminates the manual feature engineering that usually takes data scientists hours.
Benchmarks show Kumo Relational outperforms standard supervised learning models on relational tasks.
Would you trust a pre-trained model to query your company data?
